blocks.text: Why project coordinators rely on Excel

You juggle many moving parts. A project coordinator often acts as the central source of truth for a team. While dedicated project management apps exist, Excel remains the most flexible tool for custom reporting. You can build a RAID log, a budget tracker, or a resource plan in minutes. It does not require a subscription for every stakeholder. It is portable and familiar.
Essential Excel tips for project coordinators

items: Use Data Validation to create drop down menus for status columns. This prevents typos and keeps your reports clean.
Freeze the top row or first column so you never lose track of headers while scrolling through long project lists.
Create named ranges for your budget or resource tables. It makes your formulas easier to read and debug later.
Apply conditional formatting to highlight tasks that are overdue or approaching a deadline.
Use the XLOOKUP function instead of VLOOKUP. It is more robust and allows you to search for data in any direction.

blocks.text: Speed matters when you are updating a status report during a meeting. Your Mac keyboard has specific shortcuts that help you navigate Excel faster. Learn these to keep your hands on the keys.

items: Fn + F2: Edit the contents of the active cell.
Shift + Space: Select the entire row.
Ctrl + Space: Select the entire column.
Cmd + D: Fill down the value from the cell above.
Cmd + T: Convert a range of data into a formal Table.

blocks.text: If a shortcut does not work, check your System Settings. Go to Keyboard > Shortcuts and look for conflicts with macOS system commands. Disable the system command to reclaim the shortcut for Excel.
blocks.title: Fixing shortcut conflicts

blocks.text: Project data grows quickly. A sheet that starts with ten rows can become a thousand rows in a month. Excel handles over one million rows, but performance drops if you have too many complex formulas. Use Tables (Cmd + T) to group your data. Tables allow you to filter and sort information without breaking your formulas. They also make it easier to add new rows while keeping formatting consistent.

items: Hardcoding values in formulas. Always reference cells so you can update data in one place.
Ignoring errors in your spreadsheet. Use IFERROR to wrap your functions and keep your reports looking clean.
Working in a single file for years. Create new versions or archive old project data to keep the file size manageable.
Forgetting to protect your sheets. Use the Review > Protect Sheet feature to prevent others from accidentally changing your formulas.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on Mac if my team uses Windows?
faq.answer: Yes. Excel for Mac is highly compatible with Windows versions. You can save your files in the standard .xlsx format, and they will open correctly on both platforms.

faq.question: What is the best way to track project tasks in Excel?
faq.answer: Use a table structure with columns for Task Name, Assignee, Status, Start Date, and Due Date. Use conditional formatting to color-code the Status column.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Excel files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit cells, or change files for you. It points at things on your screen and explains how to perform tasks yourself.
